contents.name: Section 11.5, metric (11.35) and Lemma 11.15 on the two-sided shift space
contents.support: Supplies the published two-symbol shift space, its metric and cylinder structure that the two-sign space is identified with through the isometry phi.

contents.name: Section 11.5, completeness and sequential compactness of the shift space
contents.support: The completeness of the bounded-sequence space is reconstructed for an arbitrary index set and specialised to Z and N; sequential compactness of the shift is consumed from the run's cm-math-dynamics page.

contents.name: Section 13.1, contraction and invariant coding for the quadratic horseshoe
contents.support: The square-root contraction on the ball B_R is the explicit local form of the nested-disk coding argument.

contents.name: Section 13.1, conjugacy of the horseshoe invariant set with the two-sided shift
contents.support: The coded set, its invariance and the conjugacy follow the textbook argument, with explicit sensitivity constant 2L.

contents.name: Section 13.2, stable and unstable manifolds and the Smale-Birkhoff homoclinic theorem
contents.support: Finite-word deviations give homoclinic orbits of the constant-code fixed points, the explicit instance of the section's homoclinic picture.

contents.name: Section 13.2, hyperbolic fixed points and transverse homoclinic points
contents.support: Hyperbolicity of the fixed points, the constructed C^1 stable and unstable curves and their transverse crossing at finite-word points.

contents.name: Section 2.4, Gronwall's inequality
contents.support: The Gronwall comparison controls the state and variational differences between the rescaled pulse flow and the delta=0 reference flow.

contents.name: Section 4.2, dependence of solutions on initial data
contents.support: The variational equation for the derivative matrix of the period map.

contents.name: Section 6.4, Poincare return maps (Problem 6.14)
contents.support: The stroboscopic map of a P-periodic system is the time-P return map; the pulse model instantiates it.

contents.name: Sections 4.6-4.7, periodic equations and period maps
contents.support: The P-periodicity conventions and the time-P map formula are absorbed into the definition of the stroboscopic map consumed from cm-math-geometry.

contents.name: Section 13.3, Melnikov's method for periodically forced planar systems
contents.reason: The page proves persistence by an explicit C^1 perturbation theorem for the discrete map rather than by a Melnikov integral; the forced-oscillator family is treated through its stroboscopic map, so the section's perturbed-homoclinic integral computation is not consumed.

contents.name: Chapter 12 and later chapters (bifurcation theory, chaos in general systems)
contents.reason: General qualitative theory beyond the coded invariant set and its persistence; no item on this page asserts general bifurcation or structural stability results.

sources.title: R. Devaney and Z. Nitecki, Shift automorphisms in the Henon mapping, Communications in Mathematical Physics 67 (1979) 137-146
sources.locator: Printed pages 137-146: the Theorem with statements i)-iv) (printed pages 138-139), Lemmas 1-3 and Propositions 1-2 (the filtration, printed pages 139-142), the coding construction in the proof of statement iii) (printed pages 142-143), Lemma 4 and Propositions 3-4 on invariant sectors and the uniform expansion factor (printed pages 143-145)

contents.name: Theorem, statements iii)-iv): for large parameters the invariant set is a topological horseshoe, and for A>A_2 it is hyperbolic and conjugate to the two-shift
contents.support: The page proves the same conclusion for the explicit quadratic family in the form F(x,y)=(y,y^2-a-x) with explicit constants, by a contraction and a coding homeomorphism rather than by the paper's filtration.

contents.name: Lemma 4 and Propositions 3-4: two invariant sectors with a uniform expansion factor for JF and JF^{-1}
contents.support: The cone invariance, expansion factor and the resulting contraction of the slope maps are the precise form of the paper's sector estimates, with invariance and uniqueness of the line fields added.

contents.name: Proposition 4: uniform lower bound on |x| on the invariant set for A>A_2
contents.support: The lower bound |x_n|>=L is proved directly from the contraction on the ball B_R; this is the explicit substitute for the paper's a priori bound.

contents.name: Proof of statement iii): coding of the invariant set by bi-infinite sequences according to which component contains successive iterates
contents.support: The coding by finite windows of symbols, with quantitative continuity and injectivity of the coding map.

contents.name: Proof of statement iv): hyperbolicity of the invariant set from the invariant sectors
contents.support: Hyperbolicity of the two fixed points and the cone membership of the constructed curve tangents.

contents.name: Statements i)-ii): escape to infinity for small parameters and containment of the non-wandering set in a square
contents.reason: The page treats the large-parameter horseshoe regime and its persistence; the small-parameter escape phenomenon is not asserted or consumed.

contents.name: The filtration construction (Propositions 1-2)
contents.reason: The page obtains the invariant set from a contraction on the coded sequence space; the filtration argument for the non-wandering set is not needed and no claim about the full non-wandering set is made.
